examples.en: My father has already entered early old age.

examples.ko: 초로의 신사가 지하철에서 자리를 양보해 주셨어요.
examples.en: A gentleman in his early old age gave up his seat to me on the subway.

examples.ko: 초로의 부부가 손을 잡고 공원을 걸어요.
examples.en: An older couple is walking through the park holding hands.

examples.ko: 머리가 희끗희끗한 초로의 선생님이 교실에 들어오셨어요.
examples.en: A gray-haired teacher in his early old age came into the classroom.

examples.ko: 초로가 되면 건강이 제일 중요하다고들 해요.
examples.en: People say health matters most once you reach early old age.

examples.ko: 그분은 초로인데도 매일 아침 달리기를 해요.
examples.en: Even though he is getting on in years, he goes running every morning.

explain: '노인'보다 아직 완전히 늙지는 않은, 늙기 시작하는 때의 사람을 말할 때 써요. 보통 '초로의 신사'처럼 사람 앞에 '초로의'를 붙여서 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for someone who is just starting to grow old, not yet fully elderly like '노인'. It usually appears as '초로의 신사' (a gentleman in early old age), with '초로의' placed before a person, mostly in writing and news.

examples.en: The subway is always packed during rush hour.

examples.ko: 주말이라 식당이 초만원이라서 한 시간 기다렸어요.
examples.en: It was the weekend and the restaurant was jam-packed, so I waited an hour.
Because of the rain, the bus was totally full.
I heard every hotel is completely full because of the festival.
I barely managed to get on the packed elevator.
The concert hall was filled to capacity, so I watched standing.

explain: '만원'보다 훨씬 꽉 찬 느낌으로, 사람이 넘치는 지하철, 식당, 공연장에 많이 써요. '초만원이다', '초만원을 이루다'로 쓰고, 반대로 사람이 없으면 '텅 비다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels much fuller than '만원' and is often used for overflowing subways, restaurants, and venues. You say '초만원이다' or '초만원을 이루다', and the opposite situation is '텅 비다' (to be empty).

examples.en: When spring comes, the trees and plants turn green.
The drought was long, so the vegetation dried up.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 초목에 맺힌 이슬이 반짝였어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, the dew on the plants sparkled.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 초목도 거의 자라지 않아요.
examples.en: Hardly any vegetation grows on this island.
I walked along a forest path full of the scent of greenery.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 초목은 모두 잠을 자는 것 같아요.
examples.en: In winter, it seems all the plants go to sleep.

explain: 나무와 풀을 한꺼번에 말할 때 쓰고, '식물'보다 글 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '나무랑 풀'이라고 하고, '초목'은 설명하는 글이나 자연 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It covers trees and grass together and sounds more literary than '식물' (plants). In everyday talk people say '나무랑 풀', while '초목' appears in descriptive writing and nature topics.

examples.ko: 보고서 초벌은 제가 오늘 안에 끝낼게요.
examples.en: I'll finish the first draft of the report today.

examples.ko: 벽을 초벌로 칠하고 하루 동안 말렸어요.
examples.en: I gave the wall a first coat of paint and let it dry for a day.
I'll send you the rough translation first.
This is only a first pass, so there are a lot of mistakes.

examples.ko: 초벌 원고를 읽고 의견을 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please read the rough manuscript and tell me what you think.
Even making just the rough version took a day.

explain: 아직 다듬기 전의 첫 작업이라 '초안', '밑작업'과 가까워요. 칠할 때는 '초벌 칠', 원고나 번역에서는 '초벌 번역'처럼 앞에 붙여 쓰고, 그다음에 다듬어서 '마무리'를 해요.
explain_en: It is the first, not-yet-polished round of work, close to '초안' (draft) or '밑작업' (groundwork). You put it before the noun, as in '초벌 칠' (first coat) or '초벌 번역' (rough translation), and the polishing comes afterward as '마무리'.

examples.en: A typhoon is coming, so the company is on high alert.

examples.ko: 아이가 안 보여서 온 가족이 초비상이었어요.
examples.en: The child was missing, so the whole family was in a state of emergency.
It's the day before the exam, so even the library feels like an emergency.

examples.ko: 마감 때문에 팀 전체가 초비상에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Because of the deadline, the entire team went on high alert.

examples.ko: 초비상 상황이라서 오늘은 아무도 퇴근 못 해요.
examples.en: It's an all-hands emergency, so nobody can leave work today.
When the flu spread, every school went on high alert.

explain: '비상'보다 훨씬 급하고 긴장된 상황이에요. 보통 '초비상이다', '초비상이 걸리다'로 쓰고, 말할 때는 회사나 집이 정신없이 바쁠 때도 조금 과장해서 써요.
explain_en: It describes a much more urgent and tense situation than '비상'. It usually appears as '초비상이다' or '초비상이 걸리다', and in speech people also use it with some exaggeration when a company or home is in a frantic rush.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 나오자 교실이 초상집 같았어요.
examples.en: When the exam results came out, the classroom felt like a house of mourning.

examples.ko: 팀이 져서 우리 응원석은 초상집이 됐어요.
examples.en: Our team lost, so our cheering section turned gloomy as a funeral.
Why is everyone sitting around like it's a funeral?

examples.ko: 친구네가 초상집이라서 오늘 저녁에 문상 가려고요.
examples.en: My friend's family is in mourning, so I'm going to pay my respects this evening.

examples.ko: 초상집에 가기 전에 검은 옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I got dark clothes ready before going to the house of mourning.
The mood was so somber that I couldn't even joke.

explain: 장례를 치르는 집을 말하지만, 요즘은 '장례식장'이 더 일반적인 말이에요. 그래서 '초상집'은 실제 장소보다 분위기가 아주 우울하고 조용할 때 비유로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 합격자 발표 날 우리 반은 초상집 같았어요.
phrases.en: On the day the pass results were announced, our class was as gloomy as a funeral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 장례가 있는 게 아니라, 분위기가 몹시 침울하고 조용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: No real funeral is involved; it describes a very glum, silent mood.

explain_en: It means a house holding a funeral, but '장례식장' is the more common word for that today. So '초상집' is mostly used figuratively for a very gloomy, quiet atmosphere rather than for the actual place.

examples.ko: 저는 요리 초심자라서 쉬운 것부터 해요.
examples.en: I'm a beginner at cooking, so I start with easy things.

examples.ko: 초심자도 따라 할 수 있는 강의예요.
examples.en: It's a lecture even beginners can follow.
This guitar is just right for beginners.
It's a course that's a bit hard for a beginner.
I signed up for the beginner swimming class.

examples.ko: 초심자의 눈으로 보면 모든 게 새로워요.
examples.en: Seen through a beginner's eyes, everything is new.

explain: '초보자'와 거의 같게 쓰지만 '초심자'는 안내문이나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '초보', '왕초보'가 더 흔하고, 반대말은 '숙련자'나 '고수'예요.
explain_en: It is used almost like '초보자', but '초심자' shows up more in notices and writing. In daily talk '초보' and '왕초보' are more common, and the opposites are '숙련자' (skilled person) and '고수' (expert).

examples.ko: 초임 교사 때는 모든 게 낯설었어요.
examples.en: When I was a new teacher, everything felt unfamiliar.
The teacher's first posting was at a small country school.
I started my first posting in Seoul, so I was very nervous.

examples.ko: 초임 때 만난 선배가 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the senior colleague I met in my first posting.
I heard this first assignment is in Busan.
My mistakes from my early days on the job are something to laugh about now.

explain: 주로 '초임 교사', '초임 시절'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 처음 맡은 자리를 말해서, 교사나 공무원처럼 발령을 받는 직업에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before another word, as in '초임 교사' (new teacher) or '초임 시절' (early days on the job). It refers to the first position someone takes up, so you hear it often for jobs with assignments, like teachers and civil servants.

examples.en: Do you believe in supernatural phenomena?

examples.ko: 그 영화는 초자연적인 힘을 가진 아이 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is about a child with supernatural powers.

examples.ko: 저는 초자연적 존재가 있다고 생각하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't think supernatural beings exist.

examples.ko: 밤에 초자연적인 소리를 들었다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said she heard a supernatural sound at night.

examples.ko: 초자연적인 이야기를 좋아해서 소설을 자주 읽어요.
examples.en: I like supernatural stories, so I read novels about them often.

examples.ko: 초자연적으로 보이는 일도 알고 보면 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: Even things that look supernatural have a reason once you find out.

explain: 자연의 법칙으로 설명이 안 되는 것을 말하며 '초자연적인 힘/현상/존재'처럼 '인'을 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요. '신비로운'이나 '불가사의한'과 비슷하지만 '초자연적'은 자연을 넘어선 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It describes things that natural laws cannot explain, and it is often used with '인', as in '초자연적인 힘/현상/존재'. It is close to '신비로운' or '불가사의한', but '초자연적' stresses going beyond nature.

examples.en: As the interview time approached, a wave of anxiety came over me.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 기다리는 동안 초조감을 감출 수 없었어요.
examples.en: While waiting for the results, I couldn't hide my nervousness.

examples.ko: 마감이 가까워지면 초조감에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: When the deadline gets close, I can't sleep from anxiety.

examples.ko: 초조감 때문에 손톱을 자꾸 물어뜯게 돼요.
examples.en: Because of my nervousness, I keep biting my nails.
Once the exam was over, even the anxiety disappeared.

examples.ko: 아이 소식이 없자 부모님의 초조감은 커졌어요.
examples.en: With no news of the child, the parents' anxiety grew.

explain: '초조함'이 더 일상적이고, '초조감'은 초조한 느낌 자체를 말해서 '느끼다', '들다', '달래다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. '불안감'보다 시간에 쫓기거나 결과를 기다리며 마음이 급할 때 잘 써요.
explain_en: '초조함' is the more everyday word, while '초조감' names the feeling itself and pairs well with verbs like '느끼다', '들다', and '달래다'. Compared with '불안감', it fits best when you feel pressed for time or are anxiously waiting for a result.

en: being half-dead; being more dead than alive

examples.en: After walking all day, I was completely worn out.
I got scolded by that senior until I felt half-dead.
After working all night, my body is wrecked.

examples.ko: 마라톤을 뛰고 초주검인 채로 결승선을 넘었어요.
examples.en: I crossed the finish line half-dead after running the marathon.
I've been pushed so hard that I'm on the verge of collapse.

examples.ko: 초주검처럼 쓰러져 자는 남편을 깨우지 못했어요.
examples.en: My husband was sleeping like a dead man, so I couldn't wake him.

explain: 보통 '초주검이 되다'로 쓰고, 몹시 지치거나 심하게 혼이 났을 때 말해요. 일상에서는 너무 힘든 일을 과장해서 말할 때 많이 쓰고, '녹초가 되다'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '초주검이 되다' for being utterly exhausted or severely scolded. In daily life people use it to exaggerate how hard something was, and '녹초가 되다' is used in a similar way.

en: accomplishing one's original intention; holding one's course

examples.en: The interviewer asked for my favorite four-character idiom, and I answered with the one about staying true to your original intention.

examples.ko: 그는 초지일관의 자세로 공부해서 결국 합격했어요.
examples.en: He studied with unwavering consistency and finally passed.
Sticking to your original aim isn't as easy as it sounds.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 초지일관 한 가지 맛만 고집해요.
examples.en: This shop has stuck to just one flavor from the start.

examples.ko: 초지일관 한 길만 걸어오신 할아버지를 존경해요.
examples.en: I respect my grandfather, who has walked a single path with unwavering consistency.
I wrote that four-character phrase about staying true to your aim and stuck it up in front of my desk.

explain: '초지일관 노력했어요'처럼 부사처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 면접이나 글에서 좋은 인상을 줄 때 잘 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '한결같다', '변함없다', '시종일관'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used like an adverb, as in '초지일관 노력했어요', and it comes up in interviews and writing when you want to make a good impression. Similar words include '한결같다', '변함없다', and '시종일관'.

en: accomplish one's original intention; hold one's course

examples.en: He stayed true to his course all his life, so he is respected.
Even if it's hard, if you hold your course, a way will open up.
Your attitude of sticking to your aim is really admirable.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번 정한 목표를 초지일관하려고 해요.
examples.en: I try to stick to a goal once I've set it.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말과 행동이 초지일관하지 않았어요.
examples.en: That person's words and actions were not consistent.
Thanks to staying the course to the end, I won the competition.

explain: '초지일관 노력하다'처럼 '초지일관'만 앞에 붙여 쓰는 일이 더 많아요. '초지일관하지 못하다'처럼 부정으로도 자주 써요. 반대로 마음이 자꾸 바뀌면 '변덕스럽다', '흔들리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is common to just put '초지일관' in front of another verb, as in '초지일관 노력하다'. It is also often used in the negative, such as '초지일관하지 못하다'. The opposite idea is expressed with '변덕스럽다' (fickle) or '흔들리다' (to waver).

examples.ko: 병원에 처음 가면 초진이라서 서류를 써야 해요.
examples.en: If it's your first visit to a hospital, it counts as a first visit, so you have to fill out forms.
For a first visit, you need ID when you register.

examples.ko: 오늘 초진 환자가 많아서 오래 기다렸어요.
examples.en: There were many first-visit patients today, so I waited a long time.
This is my first visit to this hospital.
At my first visit, the doctor asked me everything carefully.

examples.ko: 초진 때 찍은 사진을 재진 때 같이 봤어요.
examples.en: We looked at the pictures taken at the first visit together at the follow-up visit.

explain: 병원 접수에서 "초진이세요, 재진이세요?" 하고 많이 물어요. 반대말은 '재진'이고, 처음 가는 병원이나 처음 받는 진료에 써요.
explain_en: At hospital reception you often hear "초진이세요, 재진이세요?" (first visit or return visit?). The opposite is '재진', and '초진' is used for a first visit to a hospital or a first consultation.

examples.ko: 며칠 밤을 새웠는지 얼굴이 많이 초췌해요.
examples.en: Maybe from staying up several nights, your face looks very haggard.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 만난 친구가 너무 초췌해 보여서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My friend, whom I hadn't seen in a long time, looked so gaunt that I was shocked.
He came out of the hospital looking haggard.
It's exam season, so everyone looks worn out.

examples.ko: 초췌하게 앉아 있는 아버지를 보니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Seeing my father sitting there looking worn, my heart ached.
She forced a smile on her drawn face.

explain: 사람의 얼굴이나 모습이 야위고 안색도 안 좋아 보일 때 써요. '수척하다'는 살이 빠진 느낌이 중심이고, '초췌하다'는 지치고 기운 없어 보이는 느낌까지 있어요. '초췌해 보이다', '초췌해지다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes a person whose face or appearance looks thin, pale, and unwell. '수척하다' focuses on weight loss, while '초췌하다' also suggests looking tired and drained. It is often used as '초췌해 보이다' or '초췌해지다'.

examples.en: Heavy rain poured down and the neighborhood was devastated.

examples.ko: 어제 모임 때문에 우리 집 거실이 초토화 상태예요.
examples.en: After yesterday's gathering, our living room is a total wreck.
Customers suddenly flooded in, and the shop was chaos.

examples.ko: 작은 실수 하나가 시스템 초토화로 이어졌어요.
examples.en: One small mistake led to the whole system being wrecked.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 간 방은 완전히 초토화예요.
examples.en: The room the kids played in is completely trashed.
It came to the brink of total destruction but was barely restored.

explain: 원래는 땅이 불타 못 쓰게 된 상태를 말하지만, 일상에서는 '집이 초토화예요'처럼 엉망이 된 상황을 과장해서도 많이 써요. 'N이/가 초토화되다', 'N을 초토화하다'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It originally refers to land burned until it is unusable, but in daily life people also use it to exaggerate a mess, as in '집이 초토화예요'. It is used in patterns like 'N이/가 초토화되다' and 'N을 초토화하다'.

en: scorch the earth; devastate; reduce to ruins

examples.en: The typhoon devastated the coastal village.
The kids trashed the living room and went out.

examples.ko: 장마가 농사를 초토화하지 않도록 미리 준비해요.
examples.en: We prepare in advance so the rainy season doesn't ruin the farming.

examples.ko: 한 번의 실수가 팀 분위기를 초토화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A single mistake can wreck the team's mood.

examples.ko: 그 댓글이 토론방을 초토화하는 바람에 글이 닫혔어요.
examples.en: That comment threw the discussion board into chaos, so the thread was closed.
The guests wiped out the whole buffet.

explain: '장소/물건을 초토화하다'로 쓰고, 피동은 '초토화되다'예요. 실제 큰 피해뿐 아니라 방이나 분위기를 엉망으로 만들었을 때도 비유로 써요.
explain_en: It takes a place or thing as its object, as in '장소/물건을 초토화하다', and the passive is '초토화되다'. Besides real large-scale damage, it is also used figuratively for messing up a room or a mood.

en: Buddha's Birthday (the 8th day of the 4th lunar month)

examples.en: On Buddha's Birthday, many lanterns hang at every temple.

examples.ko: 올해 초파일에 가족과 함께 절에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This year on Buddha's Birthday, I'll go to a temple with my family.
When Buddha's Birthday comes, the streets become bright with lanterns.
It was the Buddha's Birthday holiday, so the highway was jammed.

examples.ko: 초파일을 맞아 등 만들기 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: For Buddha's Birthday, I tried making a lantern.
The eighth of the fourth lunar month is a day off.

explain: 음력 4월 8일을 말해요. 달력에는 공식 이름인 '부처님오신날'로 나오고, '석가탄신일'도 같은 날을 가리켜요. '초파일'은 사람들이 예전부터 입말에서 많이 쓰는 이름이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the 8th day of the 4th lunar month. Calendars list it under the official name '부처님오신날', and '석가탄신일' points to the same day. '초파일' is the name people have long used in everyday speech.

examples.en: This is my first time on this road, so I turned on the GPS.
It's a road I've never been on, so I left plenty of time.
This is my first visit to Seoul.

examples.ko: 초행인 사람도 쉽게 찾을 수 있게 표지판이 많아요.
examples.en: There are lots of signs so even first-time visitors can find it easily.
On a first visit, the way is unfamiliar to everyone.
Even though it was your first time, you found the place right away.

explain: 길을 물을 때 "여기 초행이라서요"처럼 자주 말해요. '초행길'로 많이 쓰고, 처음 만나는 사람은 '초면'이라고 해서 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: People often say it when asking for directions, as in "여기 초행이라서요" (this is my first time here). It is commonly used as '초행길', and it pairs nicely with '초면' (meeting someone for the first time).
